question: For the experimental Claw update flow, should capability escalation require a separate explicit confirmation in the eventual CLI apply contract, or is a single exact `planIntegrity` confirmation intended to approve both content and capability changes?
rationale: The planner deliberately exposes `requiresDistinctConsent`, but the present human CLI wording binds all changes to one integrity token; this is an externally visible security/UX contract that cannot be resolved from implementation details alone.

options.title: Require distinct capability acknowledgement
options.body: Keep `planIntegrity` as the whole-plan binding token and require the apply slice to demand an additional explicit acknowledgement whenever an escalation record is present.

options.title: Adopt combined confirmation
options.body: Document that one exact plan-integrity confirmation intentionally approves all disclosed capability and content changes, then remove wording that implies a separate consent requirement.

recommendation.title: Require distinct capability acknowledgement
recommendation.body: Keep `planIntegrity` as the whole-plan binding token and require the apply slice to demand an additional explicit acknowledgement whenever an escalation record is present.
